EX01.title: A booking agent times out after commitment
EX01.situation: A customer authorises one booking. The provider accepts it, but the network drops the response. The customer asks the agent to stop.
EX01.pour_review: A review may examine perceivable progress text, keyboard-operable controls, understandable errors and compatibility with assistive technology.
EX01.remaining_problem: A labelled Stop button and an accessible timeout message do not establish whether the booking exists, whether cancellation reached the provider or whether retrying will create a duplicate.

application.Legible: Show Outcome unknown, booking check in progress rather than declaring failure or completion.
application.Governable: Stop new work, display cancellation-request status and disclose effects that may already have committed.
application.Interpretable: Explain what is known from provider events and why retry is currently withheld.
application.Robust: Reconcile using an operation identifier and the provider’s actual idempotency/lookup support; handle late events and partial effects.
application.Satisfactory: Restore a correct travel outcome with limited customer checking and no avoidable duplicate cost.

EX01.why_additional: LGIR+S asks about the remote operation and its consequences, not just whether the message and button are accessible. This makes the recovery requirement more explicit.
evaluation: Inject a timeout after the provider commits and then replay the response.
Verify no blind duplicate retry and inspect the actual provider/operation evidence.
Test cancellation status through the supported AT and compare total customer recovery effort.
EX01.limits: The case does not establish payment-provider guarantees, legal refund rights or automatic reversal. Tests belong in an authorised sandbox.

EX02.title: A procurement agent reads a hostile supplier document
EX02.situation: An employee delegates a bounded comparison of supplier proposals. An external PDF contains instructions to disclose internal pricing and place an order above the authorised budget. A sub-agent also retains a stale permission display.
EX02.pour_review: A review may examine readable document access, navigable comparison controls, clear labels and exposed interface semantics.
EX02.remaining_problem: The document can be accessible while its embedded instructions remain untrusted. Interface access does not supply a complete instruction-authority or tool-permission model.

application.Legible: Show actual current access, budget and supplier scope, including what data is not available.
application.Governable: Enforce recipient, spending and write limits outside generated instructions and propagate them to sub-agents.
application.Interpretable: Explain the blocked request as a conflict with actual authority without exposing secret policy details.
application.Robust: Treat retrieved text as data, test indirect injection and recheck effective permission at each action boundary.
application.Satisfactory: Continue the authorised comparison and leave the employee a useful, inspectable recommendation without turning every step into an approval prompt.

EX02.why_additional: The added lens makes delegation and the authority boundary explicit, including sub-agent propagation and scope revocation. A prompt that says be careful is not the enforcement mechanism.
evaluation: Insert an adversarial instruction in a sandbox document and revoke a capability mid-task.
Inspect attempted tool calls and actual enforcement, not only the model’s verbal refusal.
Check that benign comparison work continues and the employee understands the remaining decision.
EX02.limits: Blocking the selected injection does not prove immunity. Legal procurement duties and information security need their own actual scope and review.

EX03.title: A research assistant creates a fast but expensive-to-check report
EX03.situation: An analyst requests a sourced briefing. The assistant generates it quickly, but some citations are outdated, one source is restricted and several statements need extensive verification.
EX03.pour_review: A review may examine headings, readable text, meaningful links, keyboard navigation and predictable document structure.
EX03.remaining_problem: The report can be accessible while its facts, provenance and total human checking burden remain unacceptable for the task.

application.Legible: Distinguish retrieved facts, synthesis, estimates and evidence gaps with accessible provenance detail.
application.Governable: Keep publication outside the existing drafting authority and offer a reviewable correction route.
application.Interpretable: Explain conflicting sources and relevant dates; do not present self-reported confidence as a measured probability.
application.Robust: Carry source identity, dates, transformations and qualifications through retrieval and export without inventing missing lineage.
application.Satisfactory: Count the analyst’s source checking, correction and recovery work in the comparison, alongside correctness and usefulness.

EX03.why_additional: LGIR+S makes accountable evidence handling and the human work transferred by automation explicit. A shorter generation time is insufficient to claim a better experience.
evaluation: Include known conflicting versions, a missing source and a restricted source in a controlled brief.
Compare actual correct task completion and total review effort against an appropriate accessible alternative.
Ask participants about usefulness and burden while preserving source errors as separate findings.
EX03.limits: This is a proposed research design, not measured time saving. Do not expose protected sources in a public briefing or infer legal currency from a new access date.

EX04.title: A long-running assistant works alongside a screen-reader user
EX04.situation: A person with a screen reader delegates analysis while editing another document. The assistant generates many intermediate events, later needs one decision and finally transfers the work to a human support route.
EX04.pour_review: A review may assess focus behaviour, status messages, names/roles/states, keyboard operation and access to the output.
EX04.remaining_problem: An announcement can be technically exposed yet create an overwhelming queue. A complete co-agency design must address attention, meaningful decision timing, continuity and handover.

application.Legible: Group routine progress into a persistent summary and clearly identify the consequential waiting-for-you state.
application.Governable: Allow pause, adjustable notification detail and a supported handover without losing valid work.
application.Interpretable: Summarise completed effects, the decision needed and the limits of the successor’s access.
application.Robust: Recover after session loss, late events and permission changes without replaying already completed work.
application.Satisfactory: Investigate interruption, orientation, memory demands and whether the person can control pace and assistance.

EX04.why_additional: The agentic lens extends the existing accessibility and cognitive-design questions to the sustained division of work between person and agent. It does not imply that WCAG encourages intrusive announcements.
evaluation: Run routine high-frequency events while the participant performs an unrelated task.
Introduce an actionable failure, then resume through a differently authorised channel.
Observe lost focus, announcement backlog, successful handover and the person’s preferred level of detail.
EX04.limits: No single notification cadence suits every task or person. Do not infer a diagnosis or universally suppress important information from a settings choice.

EX05.title: An email agent reaches an irreversible send boundary
EX05.situation: A manager authorises drafting a supplier response. The agent revises recipients and wording, then offers an Undo button after sending. The mail service cannot reliably retract delivered messages.
EX05.pour_review: A review may examine understandable recipient fields, accessible confirmation controls, error prevention and perceivable send status.
EX05.remaining_problem: The meaning of draft authority, changed approval scope, external delivery and supposed undo must be tied to actual capabilities and effects.

application.Legible: Clearly separate draft, queued, sent and delivery/outcome states; identify the service responsible.
application.Governable: Require the actual authority needed for sending and recheck material changes; disclose the limits of retraction before commitment.
application.Interpretable: Preview material recipients, attachments and effects in a concise accessible form rather than asking for blind approval.
application.Robust: Bind approval to the intended version and prevent duplicate send on timeout/retry; protect concurrent edits during restoration.
application.Satisfactory: Preserve confidence and dignity through truthful correction options rather than a reassuring but false promise of reversal.

EX05.why_additional: The added lens makes authorisation and external irreversibility part of the task contract. An operable Undo button cannot itself establish that the effect is reversible.
evaluation: Change recipients after preview and verify the original approval is not reused.
Simulate send acceptance with a lost acknowledgement and check duplicate prevention.
Attempt recovery after a concurrent edit and inspect disclosure of residual effects.
EX05.limits: Use a test mail system. A compensating message does not erase delivery, disclosure or downstream reliance on the original message.

EX06.title: A travel agent optimises price but misses the actual goal
EX06.situation: A traveller requests a cheaper journey with an accessible transfer, manageable connection time and a preferred assistance arrangement. The agent returns a cheaper confirmed booking that violates a material requirement.
EX06.pour_review: A review may assess the accessible search, selection, booking and confirmation interfaces, including errors and complete processes.
EX06.remaining_problem: The agent’s optimisation target and interpretation of intent need evaluation in addition to the interface. A booking ID is not sufficient evidence of the traveller’s intended outcome.

application.Legible: Keep the operative goal and material constraints available throughout replanning.
application.Governable: Do not silently trade away a stated access requirement; obtain the necessary decision for a material change.
application.Interpretable: Explain which constraints are verified, assumed or unavailable and the consequences of each option.
application.Robust: Handle unavailable or changing supplier evidence and preserve the chosen constraints across integrations.
application.Satisfactory: Judge success against the complete travel purpose, appropriate time/effort and the traveller’s account of whether the option is usable.

EX06.why_additional: LGIR+S directly asks whether an agent’s plan and outcome preserve the person’s goal. This adds specificity to agent optimisation; it is not evidence that POUR prevents task-oriented evaluation.
evaluation: Create test options where the lowest price conflicts with a required transfer feature.
Check actual constraint retention through replanning and final booking records.
Evaluate complete journey feasibility and the person’s verification burden without inventing supplier guarantees.
EX06.limits: The case is fictional. Actual access arrangements and supplier commitments require current evidence; a model-generated itinerary cannot certify them.

EX07.title: An employee challenges an agent-assisted support decision
EX07.situation: An agent summarises workplace support requests for a human team. One summary omits a material preference, the alternative contact channel requires repeated disclosure, and a survey reaches only people who completed the process.
EX07.pour_review: A review may examine accessible request forms, understandable messages, navigation and compatibility with AT.
EX07.remaining_problem: Background summarisation, affected-person remedy, unequal service routes and exclusion from experience evidence need explicit attention beyond the form’s interface.

application.Legible: Identify the agent-assisted summary and make its relevant evidence and limits available to authorised people.
application.Governable: Keep actual human decision authority and give the employee a suitable correction route without privileged tool access.
application.Interpretable: Explain material factors and distinguish an unverified summary from an adopted decision.
application.Robust: Preserve context, permission and corrections through handovers so the wrong summary is not silently reused.
application.Satisfactory: Examine dignity, privacy, chosen assistance and reasons for dissatisfaction, including people who abandoned or could not start.

EX07.why_additional: The added lens connects the agent’s influence to actual affected people, correction and complete experience evidence. A positive score among completers cannot stand in for everyone’s experience.
evaluation: Introduce a known summary error and submit a correction through another access route.
Inspect who can act on the correction, what status is visible and whether sensitive details are repeated unnecessarily.
Compare participation and exclusion across channels; keep favourable ratings and serious barriers separately visible.
EX07.limits: No real employee decision, legal conclusion or participant finding is supplied. Do not infer diagnoses, automate consequential employment decisions from this example or publish sensitive support records.

EX08.title: A provider change preserves syntax but changes behaviour
EX08.situation: A service swaps its foundation model. API calls still validate, but the new model interprets scope differently, asks for excessive confirmations and produces more status interruptions.
EX08.pour_review: A review may assess interface behaviour and access after the change, including keyboard and status-message regressions.
EX08.remaining_problem: Model/provider changes also affect delegated behaviour, authority handling, evidence use and the effort required for supervision; interface checks alone do not establish those properties.

application.Legible: Keep supported model/tool versions and meaningful capability changes inspectable.
application.Governable: Retest enforcement and intervention independently of the model’s verbal compliance.
application.Interpretable: Compare goal interpretation, uncertainty and policy explanations in repeated scenarios.
application.Robust: Use versioned behavioural, adversarial, recovery and accessibility scenarios with an explicit affected-release decision.
application.Satisfactory: Compare total human burden, outcomes and user accounts, including regressions hidden by aggregate accuracy.

EX08.why_additional: LGIR+S provides a specific change-assurance scope for model-mediated work. Protocol compatibility and decoupled state are useful design choices, not proof of unchanged experience.
evaluation: Run the same defined task and failure scenarios on the old and candidate supported combinations.
Inspect actual tool effects, policy conflicts, notification load and intervention opportunities.
Report distributions, failures, uncertainty and affected groups; do not approve solely from a schema check or average score.
EX08.limits: No model benchmark was run. Results from one supported combination cannot be generalised to every provider or future model.
